children: The New Taiwan dollar will likely rebound after its recent slump, Goldman Sachs analysts say in a research note. The currency underperformed regional currencies, weakening by around 2.5% against the U.S. dollar. The weakness has been driven by the global correction in AI-focused equities in recent weeks, which prompted US$26 billion of net foreign equity outflows from Taiwan in October, the economists note. Meanwhile, Brent oil continued to climb, further worsening Taiwan's trade balance. Still, GS thinks these factors are temporary and remains bullish on the Taiwan dollar beyond the near term. "Upward revisions to growth, continued strong current account surplus, the strength of the AI boom, and a more hawkish Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) outlook all support" the New Taiwan dollar, they add. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
